title: Vacuum chuck apparatus for wet processing wafers

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, not a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet and pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which uses pneumatic actuation for gripping and releasing, not a displaceable magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes or magnetic fields.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use a displaceable magnet or pole shoes with specific contact surface angles relative to a displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, not a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck system that uses vacuum to hold a workpiece, not magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not have a displaceable magnet with a displacement direction.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes or magnetic fields.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with beveled active structures.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with projections for directing magnetic fields.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with projections and recesses.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.quote: In this case, eaves 23 of the head 1 are used to determine the relative position of the head 1 with respect to the wafer 7.
features.note: The reference describes 'eaves' on the vacuum chuck head used for positioning a wafer, which is analogous to a positioning device, but it is for a vacuum chuck, not a magnetic gripper, and the workpiece is a wafer, not necessarily ferromagnetic.

coord.heading: Detailed Description Of The Preferred Embodiments

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes or magnetic poles.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which uses a pneumatic system to evacuate and pressurize for gripping and releasing, not a displaceable magnet.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not explicitly mention any position sensors for gripping/release or workpiece sensors.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.quote: One end of the holder 2 is shaped to form a nozzle 17 to be fixed to the hydraulic conduit 6 (not shown).
features.note: The reference describes a nozzle for connecting to a hydraulic conduit (supply line), but does not mention a receptacle for a workpiece sensor.

coord.heading: Detailed Description Of The Preferred Embodiments

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: The chuck is fixed to an arm 26 which is movable to the left and right, and up and down.
features.note: The reference describes the vacuum chuck being fixed to a movable arm, which functions as a manipulator, but it is not explicitly described as a dedicated 'manipulator interface' on a magnetic gripper.

coord.heading: Detailed Description Of The Preferred Embodiments

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use magnetic fields and therefore does not require magnetic shielding.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with projections.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe a receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with beveled active structures.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This reference describes a vacuum chuck, which does not use pole shoes with beveled active structures.

overall.why: This reference describes a vacuum chuck for handling semiconductor wafers in wet processing, which is fundamentally different from a magnetic gripper and does not disclose any of the core features related to magnetic gripping.
